question: True or false: of two memories equally strong today, the more recent one will fade more slowly?
answer: False. The older one fades more slowly. Forgetting is fastest just after learning and slows with time, so a memory that has already lasted sits on the flat part of its curve. Adolf Jost stated this in 1897. A fact from years ago that is as clear as last week's is the safer bet.
move: What has lasted a long time has already passed the tests that remove most things.
trap: Assuming fresh means firm, because new memories feel vivid.
reference: Wixted, The psychology and neuroscience of forgetting, Annual Review of Psychology, 2004
